title: Debug logs, exception traces, checkpoints, monitoring, and production diagnosis
objectives: Use a targeted debug log / trace flag instead of org-wide FINEST.
Read an exception trace to the first application frame and know governor exceptions are unhandleable.
Place checkpoints for heap and variables when System.debug would flood the log.
Diagnose production via monitoring and LAB_ reproduction, not live customer DML.
diagnostic_question: UNABLE_TO_LOCK_ROW is intermittent in production. Someone left FINEST on for every user. How do you use debug logs, exception traces, checkpoints, monitoring, and production diagnosis without making it worse?
definition: Debug logs record one request's Apex, SOQL, DML, and callouts when a trace flag is active. Exception traces are the stack to the throwing line. Checkpoints snapshot variables and heap at a line. Monitoring is Apex Jobs, Scheduled Jobs, the debug-log list, and official limit usage. Production diagnosis reproduces with LAB_ data and the smallest trace. ([Debugging Apex](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_debugging.htm); [Execution Governors and Limits](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_gov_limits.htm); [Apex Developer Guide](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_dev_guide.htm))
why_it_matters: Org-wide FINEST fills log allocation and still misses the failing user. Interviewers want a trace-flag plan, a stack read, a checkpoint, and a rule against experimenting on customer rows.
sixty_second_explanation: Flight data recorder: a debug log is the FDR for one flight when the tower sets a trace flag. Exception traces are the black-box stack—read down to your LAB_ class, not only LimitException. Checkpoints are freeze-frames of the gauges. Monitoring is the airport board: Apex Jobs, daily async, failed schedules. Production diagnosis reconstructs the flight in a sandbox with LAB_ passengers. Turn the FDR off when the flight is done.
deeper_explanation: Debugging Apex covers debug logs, Developer Console, and checkpoints. Logs consume an org allocation; they are not infinite. Set a trace flag on a user or class with a level and an expiration. Org-wide FINEST is a last resort. ([Debugging Apex](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_debugging.htm))

Exception traces list the call stack. Governor exceptions cannot be handled (governors page). Read the first frame that is your code. DmlException includes row-level errors. Do not log secrets. ([Execution Governors and Limits](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_gov_limits.htm))

Checkpoints snapshot variables and heap at a line in a sandbox. They beat 200 System.debug lines that blow the log. They are not a production APM. Reverify Console clicks on the current Debugging topic.
Monitoring: Apex Jobs, Scheduled Jobs, CronTrigger, AsyncApexJob, debug-log list, REST limits for DailyAsyncApexExecutions (APEX-011). Email deliverability is APEX-014. Event usage is APEX-012.

Production diagnosis: reproduce in sandbox with LAB_ data and a targeted trace flag. Do not add System.debug to production as the first move. Do not DML customer rows to see. Capture user, time window, and request. Expire the trace flag.

mental_model.analogy: A flight data recorder: debug logs are the FDR for one flight, exception traces are the black-box stack, checkpoints are freeze-frames of the gauges, monitoring is the airport board, and production diagnosis is a sandbox reconstruction—not yanking cables on a live airliner.
useful_mapping: FDR for one flight → debug log for one request
tower enables recorder → trace flag with expiration
black-box stack → exception trace to your LAB_ line
airport board → Apex Jobs / Scheduled Jobs / limits
org-wide FINEST → leaving every FDR running until the tape is full
where_it_breaks: Log retention hours/counts are org allocations—do not invent the number; look at Setup.
Checkpoints are a Console tool, not an always-on production profiler.
The FDR analogy does not encode Event Monitoring product SKUs.

mermaid.structure:
flowchart TD
  Symptom[User-reported failure] --> Scope[Time user and request]
  Scope --> Mon[Monitoring: Apex Jobs Scheduled Jobs limits]
  Mon --> Flag[Trace flag on that user or class with expiry]
  Flag --> Log[Debug log for one request]

  Repro --> Off[Expire the trace flag]

claims.claim: Debug logs capture a request when a trace flag is active. Use targeted flags with expiration; logs consume org allocation.
Governor exceptions cannot be handled. Exception traces still point at the application frame that exhausted the limit.
Checkpoints snapshot variables and heap at a line and are preferable to flooding System.debug.
Async failures are monitored via Apex Jobs / AsyncApexJob. Production diagnosis belongs in a sandbox with LAB_ data, not unplanned customer DML.

changed_in_release: Reverify Developer Console checkpoint UI and debug-log retention on the Summer '26 Debugging Apex page. Do not invent retention hours.
unresolved_uncertainty: Exact maximum stored debug logs / retention hours are org allocation—Needs verification in Setup, not invented here.
Event Monitoring / Shield SKU capabilities are neighboring products, not this lesson's default toolkit.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: I set a targeted trace flag, read the debug log and exception trace to my LAB_ frame, use checkpoints in sandbox for heap, watch Apex Jobs for async, and reproduce with LAB_ data. I expire the flag. I do not leave org-wide FINEST on.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I start with monitoring: is it a failed Queueable, a scheduled miss, or a sync click? I flag one user or class. I read SOQL/DML/LIMIT_USAGE in the log and the stack's first application line. Governor exceptions are unhandleable—I redesign, I do not catch. Checkpoints replace debug spam. Production: no customer DML experiments, no secret logging. I turn the flag off.

when_to_use: When a single user request fails: a targeted debug log / trace flag, not org-wide FINEST.
When the toast is generic: read the exception trace to the first LAB_ frame.
When heap or a collection looks wrong: a checkpoint in sandbox instead of serializePretty in a loop.
When jobs sit Holding or fail: monitoring Apex Jobs before another deploy.
When the bug is production-only: production diagnosis via LAB_ reproduction and the smallest flag.
When LIMIT_USAGE in the log must be compared to Execution Governors and Limits, not a blog.
when_not_to_use: Do not leave org-wide FINEST debug logs running as a lifestyle.
Do not diagnose by DML on customer production rows.
Do not catch governor exceptions because the trace named a limit.
Do not flood System.debug in a 200-row loop and call it monitoring.
Do not invent log-retention hours; look at Setup allocation.
Do not treat checkpoints as a production always-on profiler.
configuration_or_code_location: REST limits resource for daily async (APEX-011).

worked_example.scenario: Sales users hit UNABLE_TO_LOCK_ROW on LAB_Inventory__c around 10:00. Someone enabled org FINEST. No production data changes allowed beyond a trace flag.

decisions.decision: Expire org FINEST; set a two-hour user trace flag on one failing user.
decisions.because: Debugging Apex: targeted logs; allocation is finite.

decisions.decision: Read the exception trace to LAB_InventoryService and LIMIT_USAGE; look for FOR_UPDATE_LOCKS_RELEASE.
decisions.because: Locking + callout (APEX-010/013) is a known pair.
decisions.rejected: Catch DmlException and retry 20 times in production.

decisions.decision: Reproduce in sandbox with two LAB_ scripts and a checkpoint on the locked list; then write a test.
decisions.rejected: Update a live customer inventory row.

configuration_or_code: Trace flag: user = failing agent, Apex = FINE, expire +2h.
Search log for EXCEPTION_THROWN, FOR_UPDATE, CALLOUT.
Sandbox checkpoint on rows.size() before Http.send.
worked_example.output: Root cause: callout between FOR UPDATE and DML. Flag expired. Test from APEX-016 locks the sequence.
verification: One captured log contains the stack to LAB_InventoryService.
worked_example.self_explanation: Small FDR, read the black box, freeze-frame in the hangar, no live-cable yank.

hands_on_lab.environment: Disposable sandbox; LAB_ service that can throw.
starting_state_checks: You will expire any flag you create
steps: Write LAB_Boom.explode() that divides by zero after a SOQL.
Set a user trace flag, run the method, download the debug log.
Set a checkpoint on the SOQL list and inspect heap/variables.
Delete/expire the trace flag; add a test that asserts the exception type (APEX-016).
guided_completion: If you cannot find LAB_Boom in the stack, you opened the wrong log.
If the flag is still active tomorrow, you failed the cleanup.
hands_on_lab.independent_challenge: Find LIMIT_USAGE rows and map two of them to the governors table (SOQL 100, DML 150).
evidence: Redacted log snippet with the LAB_ frame
Screenshot or note that the flag expired
stop_recovery_cleanup: Delete LAB_Boom if it is not needed
hands_on_lab.limitations: Does not prove Event Monitoring SKUs or production log download policies.

decision_table.signal: One user can reproduce a sync error.
decision_table.choose: User-level trace flag with a short expiry; read that debug log.
decision_table.why: Debugging Apex: targeted flags; allocation is finite.

decision_table.choose: Apex Jobs / AsyncApexJob first; then a class-level flag if you need a log.
decision_table.not: Only System.debug in the trigger that enqueued it.
decision_table.why: Monitoring boards catch async; the parent request log is gone.

decision_table.signal: You need collection contents at line 88.
decision_table.not: JSON.serializePretty in a 200-row loop in production.
decision_table.why: Checkpoints exist to avoid log floods.

decision_table.signal: Stack says LimitException: Too many SOQL queries.
decision_table.choose: Find the first LAB_ frame; redesign the query (APEX-007/018). Do not catch it.
decision_table.why: Governors: unhandleable; the trace still names your loop.

decision_table.signal: Leadership wants a 'quick prod update to see'.
decision_table.choose: Refuse; reproduce with LAB_ data in sandbox.
decision_table.not: Anonymous DML on a customer Opportunity.
decision_table.why: Production diagnosis does not experiment on customer rows.

decision_table.signal: You need a daily async number during an incident.
decision_table.choose: REST limits / governors page (250,000 or licenses×200).

limitations: Log retention counts are not invented here.

security_notes: Never System.debug session IDs, named-credential secrets, or full PII payloads.
Downloaded logs are data—treat them as confidential.
Trace flags are privileged; expire them.
common_mistakes: Reading only the governor name, not the LAB_ frame.
Debug in a loop that blows the log.

interview_questions.question: How do you take a debug log without harming the org?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Set a user or class trace flag with a short expiration and the lowest level that shows the bug. Download that request's log. Expire the flag. Do not leave org-wide FINEST on.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I explain allocation is finite. I match the flag to the failing user. I look at EXCEPTION_THROWN and LIMIT_USAGE. I never log secrets. I cite Debugging Apex, not a blog of log-retention hours I cannot see.
interview_questions.example: Two-hour user flag on the agent who hits the inventory error.
follow_ups: What if the user is a site guest?

interview_questions.question: How do you read an exception trace in an interview?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: I start at the throw, walk to the first LAB_ class/method/line, then map governor names to the official table. I do not stop at System.LimitException.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I mention unhandleable governors. I look at DmlException row errors. I connect the frame to a test I will write (APEX-016). I do not invent line numbers I did not see.
interview_questions.example: LAB_InventoryService.decrement line 42 under a LimitException: Too many SOQL queries.
follow_ups: What if every frame is Salesforce internal?

interview_questions.question: When do you use a checkpoint instead of System.debug?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: When I need heap or collection contents at a line and debug would flood or truncate the log. Checkpoints are a sandbox Console tool, not production APM.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I set the checkpoint, run the LAB_ script, inspect, remove it. I do not serializePretty Trigger.new in production. I reverify Console steps on the Debugging topic.
interview_questions.example: Checkpoint on the FOR UPDATE list before a callout.
follow_ups: Heap vs CPU in the snapshot?
weak_answer_warnings: 200 debugs as a badge of thoroughness

interview_questions.question: Queueable failed at 02:00. Walk monitoring then logs.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Apex Jobs first for status and exception. Then a class-level flag if I need a body log on the next run. I do not look at yesterday's UI click log.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I query AsyncApexJob. I check daily async remaining if the error is capacity. I may run the batch in sandbox with LAB_ data. I expire flags. I connect APEX-011.
interview_questions.example: Failed LAB_ArchiveBatch execute in Apex Jobs with a QueryException.
weak_answer_warnings: Only adding debug to the trigger that enqueued it

interview_questions.question: What do you refuse to do during production diagnosis?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: DML on customer rows to see, org-wide FINEST, logging secrets, catching governors, and leaving flags on.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I write a sandbox repro and a test. I use the smallest flag if I must see production once. I treat downloaded logs as confidential. I will say Needs verification for retention hours rather than invent them.
interview_questions.example: Manager asks to flip a live Opportunity stage to reproduce.
tradeoffs: One production log vs sandbox first
follow_ups: Who approves a prod trace flag?

interview_questions.question: No log appeared after the user clicked.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Wrong user, expired flag, allocation full, or the work was async. Check Apex Jobs and the flag list before rewriting code.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I confirm the user Id on the flag. I clear old logs if allocation is full—after saving the useful ones. I do not enable FINEST for everyone as the fix.
interview_questions.example: Flag was on a sandbox user while they reproduced in production.

interview_questions.question: How do logs relate to governors and transactions?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: A log is one transaction/request. LIMIT_USAGE maps to the official per-transaction table. A new Queueable execute is a new log if flagged. Rollback still shows DML that later undid.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I connect APEX-010: you may see DML then EXCEPTION then no commit. I will not claim logs reset governors. I cite 100 SOQL / 150 DML / 10 sendEmail / 100 callouts / 120 s from the governors page when I see those rows.
interview_questions.example: Log shows 150 DML then LimitException; savepoint rollbacks counted as DML (APEX-010).
follow_ups: Does a log include after-commit events?
weak_answer_warnings: Treating the log as a second governor table with different numbers

interview_questions.question: How do you keep diagnosis from becoming permanent debug code?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Time-boxed flags, checkpoints instead of leftover debugs, tests that lock the repro, then delete the noise. Monitoring boards stay; FDR lines do not.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I fail a PR that adds System.debug(user) in a loop. I ask for a test from APEX-016. I keep Apex Jobs monitoring. I do not ship FINEST.
interview_questions.example: PR removes 40 debug lines and adds a test named decrements_without_callout_under_lock.
